subject: Welsh Idiot
author: BootlegGiant
body:
So after a long think about skate I have decided to buy it, I cant rent it as the closest rental is Bangor and to much hassle and all that, anyway I went to the city straight after work and trawled around the retail park, I went to Currys, PC World and Blockbusters and could find it no where, at this point I was cursing at my luck so I  got out my Nokia N95 with sat nav 5 megapixel camera and a copy of Burnout on the memory card and went onto Play.com (handy thing mobile internet) and guess what I saw, yes Ezo skate is not released in the UK until 12/10/07 thats right next month I feal such an Idiot, so I came home with my tail between my legs downloaded the Demo and urm yes its Ok, I like the camera angle, it kinda sucks that there is a time limit to it, I can ollie kick flip to dark slide, nollie off the rail, I can do a coffin under most of the objects, I can do a few moves but for the life of me I cant manual when I am moving, but it has put me in a mood for a bit of TH, anyway I will tell you what i think of it when it reaches our shores in a months time (I am a Idiot)

Some retail outlets have released Halo 3 to the public namely Argos and Tesco and apparently microsoft dont like it (no kidding)

subject: apologies I forgot this part
author: oO EezO Oo
body:
I haven't played any of the Tony Hawk games in a while, maybe about two or three releases ago, can't remember which one it was.  What’s really different about skate.  is the controls and how you do tricks in the game.  RT controls your right hand (grabs) LT your left hand, X pumps your left foot, A pumps your right foot and 90% of your trick controls is off of the right analog stick.  Down up to ollie, up down to nollie etc etc.  It took me a good hour to wrap my head around it and get to the point where I could really start setting up some good runs of tricks and grinds.  Once I got that down the game was a blast to play.  The demo on the marketplace is pretty good but I'd run it at least 2 times to give yourself some time to get used to the controls.  I have no problems recommending it as a rental for sure.  There are no tricks to unlock so everything is open from the beginning you just have to figure out how to pull em off.  Just skating around the city you could kill a few hours easily and the game puts in subtle hints when you come across a nice area with good terrain by cranking up the music a notch or two.  Good soundtrack too by the way.  Crashing is a blast.

" Ooh ooh ooh......VERTICAL.......sweeeeeeeeeeet! "
